page: Amazon Web Services m8a.24xlarge is a general-purpose, 8th-generation instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and AMD EPYC 9R45 processors. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 96 dedicated physical cores running at up to 4.5 GHz, without multi-threading per core (1 thread per core). It is configured with 384 GB of 6 GHz DDR5 memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. Per-core cache allocations include 48 KB of L1 data cache and 1 MB of L2 cache, supported by 32 MB of L3 cache, with hardware support for vector and matrix instruction extensions including AVX-512, VNNI, and BF16.

Benchmark results place the m8a.24xlarge predominantly within the top 10% tier across compute and memory evaluations. It achieved a Geekbench multi-core score of 31,548 and a PassMark CPU score of 141,427.23, demonstrating strong parallel processing capabilities. Memory subsystem benchmarks show high bandwidth, achieving 516.53 GB/sec uncached large-block read throughput and 229.23 GB/sec write throughput. The instance also handles memory-intensive workloads effectively, recording 254.31 million Redis SET operations per second and 114.49 GB/sec static web serving throughput.

From an infrastructure standpoint, the instance delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 40 Gbps, zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, and contains no local storage, requiring network-attached storage solutions such as EBS. In CPU-based LLM inference, the 96-core configuration processes 70B model prompts at 39.76 tokens/sec and generates text at 9.79 tokens/sec, both ranking in the top decile for CPU inference, although small model token generation falls into the middle 50% tier.

The m8a.24xlarge offers high computational density per host for large multi-threaded workloads without GPU requirements. Its resource profile fits large-scale enterprise applications, high-throughput microservice backends, in-memory caching systems like Redis, relational databases, Clang-based software compilation pipelines, and multi-threaded data processing tasks.
description: Amazon Web Services m8a.24xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 96 dedicated x86_64 cores driven by AMD EPYC 9R45 processors at up to 4.5 GHz. Built on the Nitro hypervisor, it couples 96 physical cores with 384 GB of DDR5-6000 memory, maintaining a balanced 1:4 CPU-to-memory ratio without hyperthreading. Benchmark evaluations place the instance in the top tier across integer processing, Clang compilation, and memory throughput, reaching 516.53 GB/sec uncached reads. The platform includes a 40 Gbps baseline network interface and lacks local NVMe storage or dedicated GPUs, relying entirely on networked storage. Its balanced architectural design makes it suitable for enterprise database backends, high-concurrency Redis instances, distributed build farms, and high-throughput web serving architectures.
